sophia_sales: Hey team — customer on the POC is seeing duplicated trace IDs in their Splunk/Datadog pipeline after we enabled the log export. Any ideas?
raj_infra: Uh — do you have an example trace id? is it the X-Request-ID or our internal trace header?
sophia_sales: They pasted one, looks like two different requests sharing the same trace id sometimes. Also sending a couple 429s from our exporter -> their ingestion endpoint.
sam_poc_admin: FYI the POC app uses a front-door nginx that sets X-Request-ID and we also pass otel.trace_id in the payload. suspect header collision.
maria_sre: If nginx and the app both set the same header without normalization we can end up overwriting. Can you dump request headers from a problem request?
sophia_sales: Pasted snippet from support console:```
Headers: {"Host":"poc.example.com","X-Request-ID":"req-7a2b","x-request-id":"req-7a2b","otel-trace-id":"7a2b7a2b...","Content-Type":"application/json"}
Response: exporter returned 429, message: \"quota exceeded\"
```
tyler_eng: That header case duplication is the smoking gun. Some of our exporters canonicalize headers to lower-case and then map X-Request-ID -> trace id if otel-trace-id missing. If both exist we sometimes prefer the first seen value. Mixed-case duplicates cause duplicate associations.
raj_infra: Also the 429s mean the downstream ingestion's rate limit is hit. We should add retry/backoff and batch smaller groups. For a POC it's fine to set export concurrency to 2 and lower batch_size.
maria_sre: Quick mitigation: rewrite headers on the Redwood side to normalize to a single header: set X-Request-ID only once and drop duplicates, then map that to otel-trace-id consistently. We can do that with an env var in the POC deploy: LOG_HEADER_NORMALIZATION=enabled and HEADER_MAP="x-request-id:otel-trace-id"
sam_poc_admin: I can push a config change in the sandbox. Which env / flag exactly?
tyler_eng: Use REDWOOD_EXPORT_HEADER_NORMALIZE=true and REDWOOD_EXPORT_HEADER_MAP=\"X-Request-ID=otel.trace_id\". Also set REDWOOD_EXPORT_CONCURRENCY=2 and REDWOOD_EXPORT_BATCH_MAX=50 for now.
sophia_sales: Sounds good. Can we also add a temp dashboard so the customer can watch successful exports vs 429s? they want a live view.
maria_sre: Console -> Observability -> Exports -> create a filter on workspace "poc-acme" and metric export.http_4xx_count, export.success_count. Add a panel for average latency too. I can share a dashboard link after I create it.
raj_infra: Long term: we should improve header dedupe logic in runtime to check header equivalence ignoring case and prefer otel-trace-id when present. Filing a tiny tech debt ticket.

(10:24) deploy-bot: Deploy started for poc-acme/sandbox-config commit sha=7f3b2
(10:26) deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded in 2m12s
sam_poc_admin: Pushed the env vars and restarted the sandbox. Will validate logs now.
sophia_sales: Thanks — customer confirmed fewer duplicates and no new 429s in last 10m. They're still worried about a few historic traces mapping incorrectly.
maria_sre: We can run a one-off log reprocess to re-associate traces where we can match by timestamp + request-id. I can run that if they give export window.
tyler_eng: Filed ENG-9521: "normalize header dedupe and prefer otel-trace-id on ingest". Assign to runtime team, priority P2 for now.
sophia_sales: Perfect. I'll update the customer and ask for the window for reprocess. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
raj_infra: If they hit any more 429s, sam — toggle REDWOOD_EXPORT_CONCURRENCY back up temporarily until we throttle on our side. But keep an eye on their quota.
sam_poc_admin: Will do.
sophia_sales: Closing this thread once I confirm reprocess window. Appreciate the quick swarm. :pray:
